solutions.latex:
The alternate angle at $Y$ is $43^\circ$, so $X$ is on a bearing of $\text{S}43^\circ\text{W}$ from $Y$.

\exfigure{710_q3_s1}

$y = -0.603(180) + 95.450 = -13.09$

The model is not useful as extrapolation of data can be unreliable, and it is not possible to have a negative pulse.
Yes, because the data was only collected from basketballers, who are known to be tall. Also, only those playing that night were measured.
When 65 pies are sold, costs for the business are covered, but no profit is made.

\$300 $-$ \$180 $=$ \$120

No, a loss of \$120 would be made.
You can’t have a height of 0 cm or weight of 0 kg.
A 15 kg weight difference would predict a 10 cm difference in height.

The correlation coefficient must be between $-1$ and $1$.

There is a positive correlation between weight and height.

Costs when $N = 600$:

$C = 1200 + 5(600)$

$C = \$4200$

Income required for \$2500 profit:

$I = \$4200 + \$2500$

$I = \$6700$

Price per dinner package $= \dfrac{\$6700}{600}$

$= \$11.16$

$= \$12$ to the nearest dollar
